name: webster
description: Production documentation for an app you built, where every claim carries its source and the ones that could not be checked say so. Merges four documentation plugins into one surface (documentation-generation, code-documentation, HADS semantic tagging, readme-doctor) and adds the half none of them had: verification. /webster:plan runs a stack detector that enumerates the real public surface with a file:line anchor on every entry, HTTP routes from Next.js App Router and Pages API, Express, Fastify, Hono, FastAPI, Flask and Go mux, plus middleware, page routes, CLI binaries, package exports, environment variables read from code rather than only from .env.example, and any OpenAPI spec, then fixes the reader and sorts the pages into tutorial, how-to, reference and explanation. /webster:write extracts reference material with the right tool instead of composing it in prose, anchors each behavioural claim as it writes, tags what it could not verify, generates an llms.txt, and records a drift manifest of the git HEAD and every cited anchor. /webster:audit replays that manifest so it can say which pages a diff invalidated instead of re-reading everything, flags anchors that no longer resolve, compares the documented surface against the real one, and runs a slop detector adapted from the redpen corpus over prose and over mermaid, d2 and dot diagrams. Six gates decide done: sourced, runnable, shaped, readable, honest and unslopped. A gate that could not be run reports not_checked with a reason and never a pass, because a false pass is the worst thing a documentation tool can produce.
